name: base-for-a-reader
scope:
SOURCES. All of them are the full spec, and this scope restates none of it. "The contract" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/BUILD-reads.md: A1 to A7, B1 to B5, C and R1 to R8 are its own numbers. Sid's decisions are in src-store/README.md and win over the contract; "entry N" is entry N of its section of 11 and 12 October. "Ruling N" is point N of "Rulings" in reads/PROGRESS.md (the folder is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/reads/); each ruling is the build session's and binds beside the contract. "The implied spec" is reads/IMPLICIT_SPEC.md: L1 to L34, F1 to F11, G1 to G7, H1 to H9, the operations A1 to A7 and B0 to B5, the matrix 1 to 6, P1 to P31, V1 to V7 and VA1 to VA7. It left P1 to P31 open; ruling N is the answer to PN. "The batch probe" and "the push probe" are reads/batch-probe/RESULTS.md and reads/push-probe/RESULTS.md; each is a probe, and no form, name or table shape comes from one. "The store's page" is src-store/softland/store/README.md, and "store rule N" is rule N of BUILD-store-module.md as that page says how it is met. src-store/CLAUDE.md binds every file. The rig, the server and Inland are examples: nothing comes from their code.

HOW THE STAGE DOC IS READ. This part changes the module. Its one operation is A7. "The state" is what the module keeps so that A7 holds.

THE HARD PART. There is one: the attempts of one batch of the microbatch gate made the same for a reader of facts, by state that Rama does not set back when an attempt fails (implied spec, "A7. The base, for a reader", with its table "What would have to be the same on a second attempt"; ruling 17). It is a part of its own for three reasons. It shares no mechanism with what a gate keeps for one act, which is the part what-the-gates-keep. It is the one thing of this build that a ruling lets end another way (ruling 17 (d)), and that other way changes rows that both later parts stand on, so it is planned and run first. And its proof is of a kind that no proof of today reaches (test-store/softland/store/README.md, "What the module's proof does not reach", its second line).

OPERATIONS OWNED. A7 of the contract, whole, as rulings 16 and 17 read it: implied spec A7, P16, P17, VA7 and the matrix "6. A batch of the microbatch gate", for the rows of the store as it stands when this part is built. Two lines of those rulings are owned by the part read-path and are not this part's: ruling 16 (3) and ruling 17 (c).

WHAT IS LEFT TO A LATER PART, AND HOW. Each row that the part what-the-gates-keep adds or changes in a microbatch layer must keep what this part proves. That part shows it for its own rows, with this part's proof. Nothing is done here ahead of it.

WHAT THIS PART MUST FIGURE OUT. Each is named by its role. The shape, the place and the mechanism of each are the plan's.
1. The state that keeps the clock of a batch for every attempt of that batch: ruling 17, its first paragraph with (a) and (b); the batch probe, B3 and B4; implied spec P17, points 4 and 5; store rule 5. What it grows by and what bounds that: the batch probe, "B3.ii cost" and B6; ruling 17 (a); SKILL.md, "Never delete data unless the spec explicitly requires it"; phases.md, the cross-phase rule on write volume.
2. How the gate's walk of one batch takes that clock, for the stamp of each act and for the 10-second rule, on every attempt: implied spec A7, "What today's code does" and the table after it; store rules 17 and 18; the store's page, "The stamp of a batch".
3. What still differs between two attempts once the clock is kept, and what therefore stays held to closing: ruling 16 (1), (2) and (5); ruling 17 (b); implied spec A7, the sentence that begins "Three things would still differ".
4. The rule of what a row of a microbatch layer may rest on, said so that the next part can hold each of its rows to it: implied spec G3; the row "A second attempt" of A6's table; ruling 18, its reason. This rule is the part's interface to what-the-gates-keep.
5. The proof: ruling 17 (d) and (e); the batch probe, B2, B5 and B7; implied spec VA7 and P17, point 1; the contract, A7, "It is tried first, with a run". And what the proofs' map then says that a pass shows and does not reach.
6. The other way, and the test that sends the build to it: the contract, A7, its last sentence; ruling 17 (d), its last sentence; implied spec A7, the table "The two things that the contract asks, against the two ways", and P16, point 4. The field "notes" says what the build session rules of it.
7. What the repair costs one run of the gate, held against the store's aims: the batch probe, "B3.ii cost"; store rule 21; implied spec, "What a gate's write costs, before and after".
8. The explanations of each thing that this part changes: the contract, "Explanations, as the tree's rules say"; src-store/CLAUDE.md. The field "explanations_to_replace" names the lines.
9. What this part does not build and does not decide: the contract, "Not in this build, by decision"; the store's page, rules 9 and 19, with ruling 16 (6).
10. What it hands to the receipt: ruling 16 (2) and (6); ruling 17 (e).

rules: R7, where this part touches the store's rules: 5, 9, 17, 18 and 19.
R6, for the words that this part makes.

the_split_in_short: Three parts, in this order: base-for-a-reader (A7), what-the-gates-keep (A1 to A6), read-path (B1 to B5, and C). Each has one hard part. The cuts that were weighed and not made. (1) By gate, as the store's module was cut. One declaration, one set of checks and one shape of row serve both gates (the store's page, "How the parts relate", its first paragraph), and both gates exist today. So a part for one gate cannot be stated as a scope that leaves the other gate true: a new store key would be known to the door and to one gate only. (2) A7 inside what-the-gates-keep. That would put two hard parts with no shared mechanism in one cycle, and the one thing that can still go another way would be run last. (3) C as a part. It plans no thing of the store, and each of its measures but the first needs the read path; it is folded into read-path. (4) read-path in two; see notes, 6.

checklist_of_the_stage_doc: Every hard part has its own part, and no trivial part is left unfolded: A7; A6, with A1 to A5 folded in; the live read through layers, shared, with the read asked once and C folded in.
Nothing duplicated: each scope points by number, by heading or by a short quoted phrase. No number, table or bound of the contract is copied into a scope.
Every operation is owned once, and together the scopes cover the contract: the field coverage_of_the_contract.
State that a later part consumes is in the scope of the part that writes it: here items 1 and 4; in what-the-gates-keep items 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7.

No design: no schema, key, placement or kind of topology is chosen by this paper. Where a ruling of the build session names one (17, 18, 19 and 22), the scope points at the ruling. The fields beside "scope" name files and risks, and each guess is marked.
No boundary was rejected for looking hard. The one that was rejected, the cut by gate, was rejected because one of its two scopes cannot be stated.
notes:
FOR THE WHOLE BUILD, to rule before any plan starts.
1. The order. base-for-a-reader is first because ruling 17 (d) can still send A7 the other way, and that way changes the rows of the base that both later parts stand on. First, its run is in before anything is built on those rows, and its build is the short one. What it costs: what-the-gates-keep must show the same for its own rows (its scope, item 9). The two parts share no mechanism, so if the build session wants A7 after what-the-gates-keep, the scopes hold with that one item moved to this part.
2. The other way of A7. Rule whether PLAN-base-for-a-reader designs "the row before" in full, or only states the stop test and what the other way would ask of each part. This stage's view is the second: if the stop is met, the plan of this part runs again, and the two plans after it are planned again where they touch a row of the base. Until this part's run of ruling 17 (d) is in, the check of PLAN-what-the-gates-keep should not be called passed.
3. A depot that holds no act. Ruling 17 names one more depot. Sid's decision F6 A, Q7 a of 7 October is "Two depots, one for each gate" (the store's page, :235). This stage reads his decision as of the depots that take acts; nobody asked him. It is a line for the receipt.
4. Rows of the store's page that word an earlier decision of Sid's, and that this build puts out of step with the code: K1 A, "The store's keys are three" (:253); F5 A, its "Where it shows" (:239); F6 A (:235). Rule once, for all three parts, how such a row is replaced. This stage's view: the "Where it shows" side changes, rows are added for the entries of 11 and 12 October, and his wording of an earlier decision is not written again as new text.
5. C. The plan of read-path gives each shape (ruling 28). Rule whether that part's build also runs the measures, or the stage "the measures of the contract's section C" of PROGRESS.md's table does; and where the measuring code lives. It is no code of the store, so not under src-store/. The tree shows two places: test-store/ beside the proofs, or this folder beside the probes.
6. One seam in read-path. If its plan grows past what one session can check, the cut that leaves two parts which each stand alone is between a read asked once (B1 to B3 as far as asked once) and a read kept live (B4, B5 and C). The first would hand the second the form of a query, the form of an answer, and the pure code that puts layers together, made so that a change can be worked out for the places that it names. This stage does not make the cut: the hard part is one, and the door's plan of one part, 171 KB, was checked by one session.
7. Plans side by side. The split allows more than the build session asked for. PLAN-what-the-gates-keep takes little from PLAN-base-for-a-reader (that part's field plans_ahead_of_builds), so the two could be written at the same time, with ruling 17 standing in for the earlier plan, and joined at the check. The risk is one walk of a batch changed by two plans. The build session's to rule.
8. Three source files start with a comment that tells whoever changes the file to read the store-module's plan of that part again: module.clj, module/streaming_gate.clj, module/microbatch_gate.clj. The plan sessions of the first two parts should be given those plans' sections on the walks. Rule whether the comment gains this build's plan.

FOR THIS PART. Nothing more.

name: read-path
scope:
SOURCES. All of them are the full spec, and this scope restates none of it. "The contract" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/BUILD-reads.md: A1 to A7, B1 to B5, C and R1 to R8 are its own numbers. Sid's decisions are in src-store/README.md and win over the contract; "entry N" is entry N of its section of 11 and 12 October. "Ruling N" is point N of "Rulings" in reads/PROGRESS.md (the folder is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/reads/); each ruling is the build session's and binds beside the contract. "The implied spec" is reads/IMPLICIT_SPEC.md: L1 to L34, F1 to F11, G1 to G7, H1 to H9, the operations A1 to A7 and B0 to B5, the matrix 1 to 6, P1 to P31, V1 to V7 and VA1 to VA7. It left P1 to P31 open; ruling N is the answer to PN. "The batch probe" and "the push probe" are reads/batch-probe/RESULTS.md and reads/push-probe/RESULTS.md; each is a probe, and no form, name or table shape comes from one. "The store's page" is src-store/softland/store/README.md, and "store rule N" is rule N of BUILD-store-module.md as that page says how it is met. src-store/CLAUDE.md binds every file. The rig, the server and Inland are examples: nothing comes from their code.

HOW THE STAGE DOC IS READ. The read path is a client of the module and no module (implied spec, "How the skill's template is adapted", "Half B is a client of the module"). "The operations" are what a caller asks of it: B0 to B5 of the implied spec. "The state" is the memory of one process, and the pushes that it holds open in Rama. It owns no durable state (H6). It adds no depot, table or query to the module (the contract's picture, "No query of the store stands between").

THE HARD PART. There is one, so the read path is one part: a read through a list of layers, kept live and shared. What a change gives an asker is what B3 puts together. What B3 puts together rests on which layers are rightful for her (B2). What is rightful is itself followed live (B4; ruling 23) and can end (ruling 24). The pushes under it are shared by askers whose rights differ (B5). And nothing that was put together is kept between two changes (R2; ruling 26). A cut between these leaves no part that stands alone once a read is live. A read that is asked once is the same putting together with no push, and is folded in. C is folded in: all its measures but the first need this part. The first entry's notes, 6, name the one seam.

OPERATIONS OWNED. B1, B2, B3, B4 and B5 of the contract, each whole, with implied spec B0; C; R1, R2, R3, R4 and R5; the read path's own proof; its explanations. What a read does in each state of the implied spec's matrix 1 to 6, and the matrix "5. A live read", whole. Of A7: ruling 16 (3) and ruling 17 (c). There is no later part: nothing is left to one.

WHAT THIS PART MUST FIGURE OUT. Each is named by its role. The shape, the place and the mechanism of each are the plan's. Item 1 is the state; items 8 and 9 with it are the hard part.
1. The read path's memory of one process: what it holds, for how long, and what it never holds. R2; rulings 25 and 26; implied spec H2 and H6; "What the runtime's process holds, and loses at a restart"; "What a live read costs"; the matrix "5. A live read".
2. Opening: what an opened read path borrows, and what holds R1. Implied spec B0, H1, H5 and H7; ruling 26; the row R1 of the table "R1 to R8, each as a thing that can be observed, or not".
3. The form of a query, how a caller hands it over, and when two queries are the same thing: B1 and B5; implied spec B1, "What must hold for every word"; the contract, "The builder chooses", its first line.
4. Each word of a query, read in a streaming layer and in a microbatch layer, with the task named for each read: B1; implied spec B1 (its three words, and the table "States that each word meets, in one layer"), F3, F4, L22 and L25; rulings 11, 12 and 29; the record as the part what-the-gates-keep hands it over. And what is turned away before any call to Rama: R3; implied spec H4 and H9.
5. Who asks, and may she see: B2; rulings 16 (3), 30 and 31; implied spec B2, whole; what no fact means, from what-the-gates-keep (ruling 6).
6. Which layers, and what is said of one that is left out: B3; rulings 8 and 9; implied spec B3.
7. What an answer holds for a place: rulings 14 and 15; R4; implied spec B3, its line on which layer won, and F9.
8. Live: B4; rulings 13, 17 (c), 23 and 24; R5; implied spec B4, whole, with H8 and F11.
9. Sharing and leaving: B5; ruling 15, its last sentence; ruling 25; implied spec B5, whole.
10. How many pushes one read opens, and what a read does when a run is very large: the contract, "The builder chooses", its last line; implied spec, "What each read costs at the least", "Worked cases" and "What a live read costs"; ruling 12, on its cost; SKILL.md, on yielding and on round trips; the push probe, Z1 to Z5 and "Not settled by these runs".
11. The read path's own words: R6; implied spec H9; each ruling above that says "a word".
12. Where the code sits and what it may require: the contract, "The builder chooses", its second line, and "Explanations, as the tree's rules say"; the door as the precedent of the family.
13. The read path's proof: implied spec V1 to V6; the rows R1 to R5 of its table; VA5, its last clause; VA7, its first sentence, through the read path; "What a pass does not show". For the four other proofs: V7 and ruling 1.

16. What this part does not build and does not decide: the contract, "Not decided" (its last line, as ruling 8 keeps it) and "Not in this build, by decision"; rulings 9, 11, 12 and 13; R8.
17. What it hands to the receipt: the contract, "Commits and the receipt", the line that the receipt opens with; rulings 8 to 13, 26 and 27, each where it says "the receipt" or "row for the queue".
